note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a Const 67; A06b Const 67; L05 Const 70(1)(a)-(d), PNG 6C): ordinary naturalisation after 8 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another (with exceptions). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generally applicable provision), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, with no further limit on a child born abroad. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Papua New Guinea, 2024
sources.said: Residence for 8 years required. ... Renunciation of foreign citizenship required (except if person is a citizen of a prescribed country and obtained permission for retention of citizenship). ... Automatic loss of citizenship by obtaining nationality or citizenship of another country by voluntary act other than marriage. Automatic loss of citizenship by exercising a right exclusive to nationals of another country or taking oath or allegiance to foreign country. Except if citizenship of a designated country is acquired and permission is requested for retention of citizenship (Australia, Fiji, Germany, New Zealand, Samoa, United Kingdom, United States of America and Vanuatu). Automatic loss of citizenship where person travels on a foreign passport (some exceptions, including with approval of minister). ... Generally applicable provision ... Registered birth in PNG on or after date of independence (16 September 1975). One parent must be a citizen or would have been entitled to citizenship on independence. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person born outside PNG on or after independence (16 September 1975). One parent must be a citizen or would have been entitled to citizenship on independence day. Birth must be registered. ... No provision ... No provision
